sections.html:
The Champaign County Clerk and Recorder files deeds, mortgages, releases, plats and other land documents. The Recorder used to be its own elected office. Voters approved a merger in 2020, and since January 1, 2022 it has been the combined Clerk and Recorder. The office goes back to 1833, when the county was organized, and its books are what a title company searches before any sale.

Land records are open to the public, though Social Security numbers, phone numbers and email addresses are redacted. The counter is open weekdays from 8 until 4:30 and closes for major holidays. On the second Wednesday of each month, doors open at 9 instead.

A standard real estate document costs $70, with no per-page add-on. That covers deeds, mortgages and releases that follow the office's formatting rules. The schedule below took effect April 1, 2025.

Recording fees by document type
Document typeRecording fee

Non-standard real estate documents$82.00

Recording fees rise by $10 on December 1, 2026, so call the office to confirm the amount before you mail a check. Plain copies cost $.50 per page. Certified copies cost $12 for the first four pages and $1 for each page after that. Government bodies do not pay the $19 Rental Housing Support fee, which lowers their total by that amount.

A deed that breaks a formatting rule is either billed at the non-standard rate or sent back. Real estate documents need the following:

  • White 8.5 by 11 inch paper, with the top 3 by 5 inches on the right side left blank.
  • No permanently bound or continuous forms, and nothing stapled or taped to a page.
  • The full name and address of the preparer, and of the place to return the document, within the text.
  • Original signatures and correct payment by check or cash.
  • For deeds, a complete name and address for where the tax bill is to be sent.
  • An associated document number for assignments and releases.

Plats have many rules of their own, so ask your surveyor. Fill in the tax bill address on the deed with care. The Treasurer's office warns that a bill can still reach the previous owner when the closing date and the recording date fall on different sides of a billing cycle.

MyDec is the Illinois Department of Revenue's free online service for transfer declarations and revenue stamps, and Champaign County runs every property transaction through it. Each deed needs a signed and dated MyDec declaration or a letter of exemption. Set up your account before closing day, because the recorder checks the declaration as part of the package.

E-recording is the quick route. Documents sent through an approved partner go over the internet, get recorded and come back digitally the same day. The approved partners are ePN, Indecomm Global Services, Simplifile, CSC eRecording Solutions and Hopdox. Fewer rejections, faster corrections and no postage are the main perks, so ask your title company or settlement lawyer whether they file electronically.

sections.h2: Illinois transfer tax on a sale
sections.html:
Illinois taxes the privilege of transferring title at fifty cents for every $500 of value, rounded up for any fraction, as stated on the transfer declaration (35 ILCS 200/31-10). If the document says the property is transferred subject to a mortgage, the unpaid mortgage balance is left out of the basis. The tax is owed whether or not the document gets recorded.

The recorder collects the tax through revenue stamps. Under 35 ILCS 200/31-15, paper stamps were to be phased out by December 31, 2025, and counties now issue electronic stamps or another form of indicia, reported through MyDec. Ask the Clerk and Recorder or your title company which local charges, if any, will appear on your settlement statement.

Section 31-45 lists deeds that are exempt. Some examples:

  • Deeds to or from a governmental body, or from certain charitable, religious or educational organizations.
  • Deeds that secure a debt, and deeds that release property held as security.
  • Deeds that only confirm, correct or supplement a deed already recorded.
  • Deeds where the actual consideration is less than $100.
  • Tax deeds, deeds of partition, and deeds given to a mortgage holder in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure.

An exempt deed may still require the declaration, so read the statute text before you skip the form.

Mid-2025 population is estimated at 209,972 in a county of about 996 square miles. Owners occupy 54.0% of housing units, the median owned home is valued at $211,500, and the median rent is $1,051 a month. Urbana is the county seat and Champaign is the biggest city, with the University of Illinois between them.

The Clerk and Recorder works from the county's Urbana offices, and the Treasurer collects the tax on those same parcels from a different office. A student rental in Champaign, a ranch house in Mahomet and a farm parcel near a village all record the same way, but their prior-owner bills and unpaid installments can differ widely. Get the PIN history from the Treasurer before the deed goes in.

Recording puts the property in the new owner's name in the land records. The tax side follows on its own track. The Champaign County Treasurer tells new owners to check their closing documents, title company or attorney to see whether tax is owed. If the bill went to the previous owner, that person must forward it, and the Treasurer will send a duplicate on request at 217-384-3743.

A seller who wants a clean exit should confirm that both installments for the year are paid or credited on the settlement statement. Unpaid taxes go into the annual sale in late October, and redemption after a sale runs through the County Clerk, so a missed payment turns into a second office visit later.

sections.h2: Military discharge papers, liens and releases
sections.html:
Besides deeds, the office accepts DD-214 military discharge papers at no charge. Bring the original, and the staff will scan it, create a permanent record and hand the original back. A certified copy later requires a government-issued ID, and discharge papers less than 62 years old are not available to the public.

State and federal tax liens and releases are recorded for $51 each. A release for a mortgage you paid off is recorded here too, and it needs the document number of the mortgage it satisfies. Before you list a house, have your title company search for open mortgages and liens so a release can be recorded ahead of closing.

If you are selling for cash and want to close quickly, ask the title company early what has to be recorded and in what order. Releases, the deed and any lien payoff are separate filings, and each has its own fee and its own paperwork.

faqs.q: What does filing a deed cost in Champaign County?
faqs.a: $70 for a standard real estate document, or $82 if it misses one of the office's requirements. Fees rise by $10 on December 1, 2026.

faqs.q: Is a MyDec declaration required before a Champaign County deed is accepted?
faqs.a: Yes. Every deed needs a signed and dated MyDec declaration or a letter of exemption, and the county runs all property transactions through MyDec.

faqs.q: Can a deed be recorded electronically in Champaign County?
faqs.a: Yes. Approved partners such as Simplifile, ePN and CSC eRecording send documents over the internet, and they are recorded and returned the same day.

faqs.q: What is the Illinois transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: Fifty cents on each $500 of declared value, with any fraction counted as a full unit, under 35 ILCS 200/31-10. A mortgage balance left in place is excluded from the basis.

faqs.q: When is the recorder's office open?
faqs.a: Weekdays from 8 until 4:30, except major holidays. It opens at 9 on the second Wednesday of each month.
